title: The State of Independent Vet Clinic Websites 2026
note: Aggregates computed from automated scans. No individual site is identified.
attribution: Free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0. Credit Clikiti with a link.
citation: Clikiti. (2026, October 15). The state of independent vet clinic websites 2026 (Q4 2026) [Report]. https://clikiti.com/research/vet/2026-q4
audience: Web agencies and freelancers selling to independent veterinary clinics
findings: Only 17% of the 138 independent veterinary clinic websites we scanned say whether they are taking new patients.
A typical site answers four of the ten questions pet owners ask before choosing (mean 3.7).
The median overall score is 77 out of 100 (mean 77).
The least-answered questions are "Are you taking new patients?" (17%), "Will my anxious pet be handled gently?" (17%) and "What does a visit cost?" (17%).
The best-answered are "How do I reach you, and when are you open?" (75%) and "What do I do if it happens tonight?" (57%).
By kind of business, the highest median score is 78 (mobile and house-call vets), against 77 for general and family practice, 76 for emergency and urgent care and 75 for specialty and referral.
72% fail "Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone" (Core Web Vitals · LCP).

agencyProblems.label: Says whether it takes new patients
agencyProblems.question: Are you taking new patients?
agencyProblems.fix: Say on the home page whether the clinic is taking new patients, with one line on what the first visit involves and what records to bring.
agencyProblems.pitch: A family new to town cannot tell from your site whether you would even see their pet.

agencyProblems.label: Fear Free or low-stress handling described
agencyProblems.question: Will my anxious pet be handled gently?
agencyProblems.fix: A short page on how the clinic handles anxious pets: Fear Free or Cat Friendly certification, quiet rooms, pre-visit calming, linked from the home page.
agencyProblems.pitch: Owners of nervous animals put off visits, and your site never tells them how you make it easier.

agencyProblems.label: A price shown: an exam, a vaccine or a fee
agencyProblems.question: What does a visit cost?
agencyProblems.fix: Publish the price of an exam and the common vaccines, or a starting price and the travel fee for house calls.
agencyProblems.pitch: "What will a visit cost?" is the question owners are most nervous to ask, and your site gives them no number at all.

agencyProblems.label: Species named, or exotics said yes or no
agencyProblems.question: Do you see my kind of animal?
agencyProblems.fix: Name the animals the clinic sees (dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, reptiles) and say plainly whether it sees exotics, on the home and services pages.
agencyProblems.pitch: Owners of a rabbit or a bearded dragon cannot tell whether you will see them, so they call someone who says so.

agencyProblems.label: Text contrast passes 4.5:1
agencyProblems.fix: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 in the theme.
agencyProblems.pitch: Parts of the site are hard to read, and it is a WCAG failure.
